summary:
Visitors to Kentucky stand under the United States federal framework on travel documents and screening. Since January 2025, Executive Order 14168 has required federal identity documents to reflect sex assigned at birth, the State Department has stopped processing the X marker, and new passports are issued only as M or F, so a trans visitor's papers may not match their presentation. Airport screening, visa discretion and the refusal of visas to trans athletes seeking entry for women's sporting events are likewise national rules that apply on arrival in Kentucky as anywhere else in the country.

Kentucky has legislated against transgender facility use in its public schools. Senate Bill 150 was enacted on 29 March 2023 when the Kentucky legislature overrode Governor Andy Beshear's veto; the statute restricts which bathrooms transgender students may use in public schools and is the single 2023 Kentucky law carrying the K-12 facility restriction. The Movement Advancement Project's equality map, which catalogs such bans state by state, lists Kentucky's 2023 K-12 facility ban among its entries.

Direct exposure for a visitor is confined by the law's setting. The restriction governs restrooms in public schools rather than commercial premises, transport hubs or hotels, so an adult trans traveller is unlikely to encounter it outside a school building. The statute nonetheless places Kentucky among the states that have enacted facility restrictions against transgender people.

Implementation runs through local school districts. In April 2023 the Kentucky Department of Education issued guidance to districts on carrying out the 2023 rules, advising them to remove sex education from the fifth-grade curriculum and to tread cautiously with the bathroom-ban provisions. A visitor accompanying a child, or entering a school site, therefore encounters a restriction administered at district level under state guidance.
tangentialFactors:
Kentucky's school-scoped restriction sits within a wider national pattern. State bathroom bans applying to trans people in K-12 schools and some government buildings are in force in nine states and one territory, with additional states imposing outright bans on facility use according to gender identity, and in some jurisdictions trans bathroom use is a criminal offence in certain circumstances. Twenty-nine states, four territories and the District of Columbia have no such ban.

Enforcement of such laws is documented. In April 2025 a trans student who announced that they were there to break the law used a women's restroom at the Florida state capitol and was arrested and handcuffed, in what civil-rights attorneys identified as the first known arrest under a state bathroom-restriction law.

Restriction is not confined to facilities. Kansas has enacted a law invalidating birth certificates and driver's licences that do not bear sex assigned at birth and barring trans residents from changing those markers, and rights groups describe the Kansas statute as a template other legislatures are following. A national legal risk assessment dated 13 July 2026 identifies Idaho as the latest state flagged do-not-travel for trans people, bringing the total to four states so designated.

Foreign governments have issued public warnings in response to the federal document and data rules. At least eight European countries, including Finland and Denmark, adjusted travel guidelines for trans and nonbinary citizens entering the United States, advisories that followed detentions of European citizens over visa issues.
localsOnly:
Senate Bill 150 also bans gender-affirming medical care for transgender minors in Kentucky. The ban took effect on 14 July 2023, when United States District Judge David Hale lifted the injunction he had issued the previous month, preventing transgender minors from accessing puberty blockers and hormone therapy.

Seven transgender children and their parents had sued to block the law. The ACLU of Kentucky called Judge Hale's ruling a temporary setback, and litigation over the statute was continuing at that point.

The 2023 facility restriction applies to transgender students in public schools and is carried out by school districts under Kentucky Department of Education guidance issued in April 2023. That guidance also advised districts to remove sex education from the fifth-grade curriculum.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether Kentucky permits gender-marker changes on driver's licences and birth certificates, and under what conditions, is not sourced in this inventory; the Movement Advancement Project maintains a state-by-state identity-document map that would resolve it.

The penalties or disciplinary consequences attached to the Kentucky school facility restriction, and whether any comparable restriction reaches adult facilities such as government buildings, are not sourced here.

The status of litigation over Kentucky's care ban after 14 July 2023, including any appeal of Judge Hale's ruling, is unresolved in this inventory.
